name: fallback-swiftshader-flag-off
description: REALISTIC-SOFTWARE-FALLBACK, FLAG-OFF path (v0.33.2.9, renamed from `fallback-swiftshader-default.json`): `softwareRasterFallback` defaults ON again now that the floor is the narrow option (3) of docs/open-graphics-decisions.md item (af), so the DEFAULT path is what the sibling `fallback-swiftshader.json` asserts. This one covers the ESCAPE HATCH — the flag turned off explicitly — because that is the arm a user (or arm A of the certified table) gets: with the floor disabled, Realistic on a software rasteriser must resolve to `QUALITY_PRESETS.realistic.weak` byte-for-byte (postprocessing true, shadowMapSize 2048, dprMax 2), i.e. the SAME preset a mid phone/iGPU gets, no floor applied. Needs the probe dev server on :5200 (`npx vite --config vite.probe.config.ts --port 5200 --strictPort`) — the resolved-settings snapshot imports `/src/scene/quality.ts`, which only a dev server serves.

steps.name: boot-splash-gone
steps.failMessage: #boot-loader still covering the screen. It is removed from the DOM only once `booting` clears, which depends on sceneReady — measured 751ms and 36604ms across two runs of the SAME scenario, so no fixed wait covers it.

steps.name: dismiss-overlays
steps.eval: try { localStorage.setItem('hdb_onboarded','1') } catch {}; const s = window.__store.getState(); s.endTour?.(); s.setOnboardingOpen?.(false); s.dismissLocationPrompt?.()

steps.name: fallback-flag-off
steps.failMessage: setFeatureFlag('softwareRasterFallback', false) did not take — the flag defaults ON as of v0.33.2.9 (item (af) option (3)), and `setFeatureFlag` only applies on a dev build or an admin session, so check the probe server is actually a Vite dev server (IS_DEV true).

steps.name: software-rasteriser-detected
steps.failMessage: The runner is not reporting a software rasteriser. This scenario is only meaningful under SwiftShader — check the browser was NOT launched with a real GPU (SHOT_GPU=1 defeats it).

steps.name: device-class-weak
steps.failMessage: deviceClass is not `weak` under a software rasteriser — `deviceClassFor` name-matching regressed.

steps.name: snapshot-resolved-quality
steps.eval: (async () => { const m = await import('/src/scene/quality.ts'); const s = window.__store.getState(); window.__q = m.resolveQuality(s.qualityTier, s.qualityOverrides, s.deviceClass, s.softwareRenderer); window.__preset = m.QUALITY_PRESETS.realistic.weak; })()

steps.name: realistic-unfloored-matches-weak-preset

waitFor.store: state.qualityTier === 'realistic' && !!window.__q && !!window.__preset && window.__q.postprocessing === true && window.__q.shadowMapSize === 2048 && window.__q.dprMax === 2 && JSON.stringify(window.__q) === JSON.stringify(window.__preset)

steps.failMessage: With `softwareRasterFallback` OFF, Realistic on a software rasteriser no longer matches QUALITY_PRESETS.realistic.weak byte-for-byte — either the floor is being applied despite the flag being off, or the weak preset itself changed. Compare window.__q against window.__preset.
